VƯỜN XA QUÊ

Vietnamese Home Food Gardens

In every home I've lived in, my dad has always had a garden. He loves spending time there. Whenever we wanted him to be in a good mood, it was always a good idea to start a conversation about his garden. What fruits are in season right now? Are any plants flowering? The garden is his pride and joy. My siblings and I sometimes joke that he cares more about his plants than us.

But my dad isn't the only one who keeps a garden. My grandpa has one in his backyard, more focused on lotuses and flowers. He's even got koi fish. My uncle grows both flowers and vegetables. My best friend's dad has a big terrace garden; he was bragging about it when our dads ran into each other at the local Home Depot.

A lot of Vietnamese dishes call for very specific vegetables to be eaten with them that can't often be substituted with the common varieties found in American supermarkets. Vietnamese cuisine also tends to be very fresh as well. This has led to a lot of families growing home food gardens that are oriented towards edible plants and herbs.

When the vegetables are in season, the aunts start cooking and hosting big Vietnamese dinners. When we have a lot of rau cải, my mom will host a huge bánh xèo night. Other families might bring their vegetables over to share. Keeping a garden takes a lot of work. Maintaining a culture abroad does too. Vietnamese communities manage to do both, together.

About this project

Family garden study, 2024 · color pencil, alcohol markers, pen, paper, digital art

This project is a broad exploration of cultural heritage and community love carried through plants, oral history, and resource sharing. I sought to capture the meaning and memories embedded within the garden beds and potted plants of my family's backyard. Through the slow act of live drawing, exchanging conversations, and trimming trees, I experienced the different aspects of the garden. For many of these plants, I grew up only knowing the Vietnamese names and the ways they were used in my family. This project includes a drawn diagram of my family's backyard with information on each of the plants, gathered through interviews and memories with my family.
